# AGENTS.md: schema-generator

Generates schema.org JSON-LD for a page type from structured input or a page's HTML, and
validates JSON-LD given inline or found in HTML. Both operations are public free tools
and take content only: no network (ADR 0021).

This folder is a self-contained TypeScript project (REx ADRs 0018 and 0024): work
here as if the rest of the REx repo did not exist. In the repo, the root `AGENTS.md`
holds the project-wide rules. Repo paths below are plain text, not links, so this file
still makes sense when the folder is copied elsewhere.

## Language

TypeScript (`language: ts` in vendoring.yaml), as ADR 0024 proposes: JSON-LD processing,
where jsonld.js is the reference implementation, and HTML parsing; the TypeScript
template is hardened here first. Its own language ADR, accepted by Jay, confirms it at
the start of its Phase 2 step.

## Contract

- Spec: [contract/openapi.yaml](contract/openapi.yaml), a generated copy. Source in
  the REx repo: `packages/contracts/openapi/services/schema-generator.yaml`.
- Types: `contract/types.ts`, generated by openapi-typescript.
- Service doc: `docs/services/schema-generator.md` in the REx repo.

Operations:

- `generateSchemaMarkup` (`POST /v1/schema-markup`): Generate JSON-LD from structured
  input or from a page's existing metadata.
- `validateSchemaMarkup` (`POST /v1/schema-markup/validate`): Validate JSON-LD given
  inline or found in a page's HTML.

For an operation marked public in Limits, the gateway exposes the same method and
path with `/v1/tools` in place of `/v1`.

## Shared schemas

These parts of the contract come from `packages/contracts/openapi/common.yaml` (in
`contract/openapi.yaml` they are inlined under `components`) and are shared with other
services. A change to one ripples to every service that uses it, so it must be
additive within `v1`, and it is made in the monorepo (see "Changes outside this
folder").

- `Url` (schema, request); also used by citation-extractor, content-auditor,
  content-extractor, engine-query, llms-txt-generator, orchestrator, sitemap-extractor,
  bus messages.
- `ValidationResult` (schema, response); also used by content-auditor,
  llms-txt-generator.
- `BadRequest` (error response); also used by answer-analysis, citation-extractor,
  content-auditor, content-extractor, engine-query, llms-txt-generator, orchestrator,
  sitemap-extractor.
- `InternalError` (error response); also used by answer-analysis, citation-extractor,
  content-auditor, content-extractor, engine-query, llms-txt-generator, orchestrator,
  sitemap-extractor.
- `UnprocessableContent` (error response); also used by answer-analysis,
  content-auditor, content-extractor, engine-query, llms-txt-generator, orchestrator,
  sitemap-extractor.

## Limits

From `x-rex-limits` in the spec (single source); stay within them.

- `generateSchemaMarkup`: public; no max duration stated yet; p99 under PT2S; no LLM; no
  outbound fetch (parses the data or HTML in the request; fetches nothing).
- `validateSchemaMarkup`: public; no max duration stated yet; p99 under PT2S; no LLM; no
  outbound fetch (parses the JSON-LD or HTML in the request; fetches nothing).

## Packages

Runtime packages this tool may use (REx conventions §16, the approved list; template
switches: none). Anything else needs Jay's approval first.

- `fastify`: HTTP server
- `@fastify/sensible`: HTTP errors and helpers
- `@fastify/under-pressure`: load shedding, readiness
- `ajv`: JSON Schema 2020-12 validation
- `ajv-formats`: formats for Ajv
- `env-schema`: config from env
- `pino`: logs (Fastify's logger)
- `@opentelemetry/sdk-node`: traces and metrics
- `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node`: HTTP instrumentation (including Node's
  built-in fetch used by the LLM SDKs)
- `cheerio`: HTML parsing of the raw page passed in (content-auditor, schema-generator)
- `jsonld`: JSON-LD expansion for validation (schema-generator)

## Rules inside this folder

- Stateless: no database, cache, bus, queue, or state kept between requests; no calls
  to other REx services.
- No auth code: the spec declares `security: []`; access is enforced in front of the
  tool (network policy, gateway).
- No network besides an LLM provider's API: never call the content-extractor, never
  fetch a page, a robots.txt, an llms.txt or a sitemap. Pages, files and their
  extracted content arrive in the request (REx ADR 0021).
- Never retry: not an LLM call (set the SDKs' own retries to 0), not a whole
  operation. Return the error (`503` with `Retry-After` when the upstream gave one);
  callers own retries.
- No import resolves outside this folder. Only the packages above, exact versions,
  committed `package-lock.json`; no `workspace:`, `file:`, `link:` or `portal:`
  specifiers and no `@rex/*` packages.
- Never edit `contract/` or this file. Files listed in `.template.json` change in the
  template, or are marked `owned` there first.
- Deterministic where possible; everything that changes the output is in the request.
- LLM calls (if any) only through the `src/llm/` adapter, reported in `usage`; tests
  run with `LLM_MODE=mock` (no keys, no network).

## Changes outside this folder

The contract, shared schemas, the limits, this tool's cache entry and `keyVersion`
(`packages/contracts/cache/policy.yaml`), the package list and the template live in the
REx monorepo. Bump `keyVersion` whenever the output changes for the same input.
The policy's `resolution` defines caller overrides per environment and per customer.

- In the monorepo: change the source in `packages/contracts` (packages: conventions
  §16), re-vendor with `scripts/vendor-contracts`, and commit source and copies together.
- With only this folder: do not edit `contract/` to make code fit. Write a change
  request in your hand-off or PR description: repo path, exact change, reason, whether
  it is additive within `v1`, and the `keyVersion` bump if outputs change. Keep coding
  against the current contract until a re-vendored `contract/` arrives.

## Scope and build order

Phase 2, step 1 of 6: language ADR (TypeScript), then JSON-LD generation and validation
from data, HTML or JSON-LD (no LLM, no network).

## Build and test standalone

Not scaffolded yet: today this folder holds only this file and `contract/`.
`scripts/new-tool` (built in Phase 1) scaffolds the rest at the start of this tool's
Phase 2 step, with `--lang` as its language ADR decides. Then these commands work (for
the language above):

```bash
cp -r services/schema-generator /tmp/schema-generator && cd /tmp/schema-generator   # any folder outside the repo
npm ci
npm run build
LLM_MODE=mock npm test
docker build -t rex-schema-generator . && docker run --rm -e PORT=8080 -p 8080:8080 rex-schema-generator
curl -f localhost:8080/healthz
```
